prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer is seated on the floor, with their draped knees and lower body in the bottom half of the frame being the closest surfaces at roughly 0.2 to 0.4 metres away. Just beyond the wearer's knees in the upper-right quadrant, at about 0.5 to 0.7 metres distance and well within arm's reach, the wearer's right hand (and a second person's hand entering from the top right in frames 2 to 5, less than 0.1 metres from the wearer's hand) hovers above a circular plate resting on the floor near the wearer's bare right foot. Across the 5 frames, the camera shifts slightly up and right between frame 1 and frame 2 as the wearer's hand moves slightly further away into the plate area, while a patterned cloth and wooden board lie flat on the floor to the upper left at roughly 0.6 to 0.9 metres. This map clarifies the three-dimensional elevation of the folded orange garment flares, the raised rim of the plate, and the height of the hands above the floor and foot that flatten out in the RGB image. However, the map is unreliable in frame 1 where the floor mat and plate on the upper left appear artificially bright (near), and in frames 2 to 5 where the bright yellow garment of the person on the far right is rendered pitch-black as if infinitely far away.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map identifies only a few fragments of the scene—specifically the hands, feet, lower body, and the circular bowl/plate in the upper right—while leaving the floor, wooden board, and left-side cloths completely unsegmented. When detected, the bowl is positioned in the upper-right quadrant at about 0.6 metres from the camera wearer, directly beneath the overlapping hands (separated by less than 0.1 metres) and just in front of the wearer's bare foot, all within easy arm's reach of both people. Across the 5 frames, the masks change erratically even though the actual scene remains largely static after frame 1: frame 1 segments only the wearer's right arm and foot as 'person', frame 2 segments only the green 'bowl' with a cutout where the hand occludes it, frame 3 groups the hands, bowl, and foot into a single pink 'person' mask, frame 4 separates the green 'bowl' from a brown 'person' mask covering the hands and foot, and frame 5 splits the lower orange-draped legs and upper-right hands/bowl into two separate 'person' masks. While frame 2 and frame 4 help isolate the circular boundary of the plate beneath the occluding right hand, the segmentation map is highly unreliable, suffering from severe temporal inconsistency, missing the wearer's torso/legs in frames 1 to 4, and conflating the plate with the hands in frames 3 and 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all 5 frames, failing to detect any body or hand skeletons despite the clear presence of the camera wearer and a second person in the RGB strip. In the actual scene, the camera wearer's lower body fills the bottom half of the frame at 0.2 to 0.5 metres, with their bare right foot extending forward to about 0.6 metres and their right arm reaching from the lower right into the upper-right quadrant to hold a small stick over a plate at 0.5 to 0.6 metres. From frame 2 through frame 5, a second person positioned just out of view to the upper right (within 0.5 metres of the plate) extends their left hand into the top-right corner of the plate, less than 0.1 metres from the wearer's right hand, while both people's heads and upper torsos remain out of view so their gaze directions cannot be seen. Because the pose estimator is entirely unreliable under this steep top-down egocentric viewing angle, heavy garment occlusion over the legs, and partial cropping of the limbs at the frame edges, it provides no spatial information beyond what is visible in the RGB frames.
